findings.issue: Task 3 has `depends_on: [1]` but `wave: 1` — same wave as its dependency. Per validator rules: 'Task with depends_on: [X] must have wave > wave of task X'. Task 1 is in wave 1, so Task 3 cannot also be in wave 1 if it depends on Task 1's `streamCompletion` and `AIProviderError.streamingError`.
findings.fix: Move Task 3 to `wave: 2` (since it depends on Task 1's streamCompletion). Alternatively, remove the dependency on Task 1 if the reduce step can be deferred — but the task body explicitly relies on `providerClient.streamCompletion` from Task 1, so wave change is the correct fix. Note this also affects Task 4's dependency on Task 3 — Task 4 is currently `wave: 2, depends_on: [1, 2, 3]`, which would then need to become `wave: 3` if Task 3 moves to wave 2.

findings.issue: Task 5 has `depends_on: []` and `wave: 2`, but tech-spec Implementation Tasks places it in 'Wave 2 (depends on Wave 1)'. The task description also says 'This task is pure HTML/JS and can run in parallel with Task 4' — meaning it does not depend on any specific Task 1/2/3 deliverable. However, placing it in wave 2 with no dependencies is inconsistent with the wave gating model: a task with no dependencies should normally be in wave 1, OR have explicit dependencies justifying its wave-2 placement. If Task 5 truly is independent, it should be wave 1; if it's intentionally gated to wave 2 for sequencing, the rationale must be explicit.
findings.fix: Either (a) move Task 5 to `wave: 1` (consistent with `depends_on: []`), OR (b) keep `wave: 2` and add `depends_on: [1]` or another wave-1 dependency to justify the wave gate. Given that Task 5 is HTML/JS only and does not consume any Swift symbols from Wave 1, option (a) is cleanest.

findings.issue: Task 4 lists `depends_on: [1, 2, 3]` and is in `wave: 2`. If Task 3 moves to `wave: 2` per the critical finding above, this depends_on chain becomes inconsistent (Task 4 in wave 2 depends on Task 3 in wave 2). The dependency graph itself is correct — Task 4 truly needs all three — but the wave assignment must be re-evaluated together with the Task 3 wave correction.
findings.fix: After fixing Task 3's wave (moving it to wave 2), promote Task 4 to `wave: 3`. Update tech-spec Implementation Tasks section if waves are renumbered.

findings.issue: Task 2 introduces a placeholder `InsightSession` stub class (item 1 in 'What to do') that exists only to make Wave 1 compile, and Task 4 then removes/replaces it. This is a workaround for cross-wave compilation that creates rework: Task 2 writes a stub, Task 4 removes it. This pattern is a code smell — it would be cleaner to either (a) defer the `TabKind.insight(InsightSession)` enum case to Wave 2 (when the real class exists), OR (b) reorder the dependency so `InsightSession` is created in Wave 1 (i.e. swap which task introduces the type). The current approach forces Task 4 to do a destructive edit on Task 2's output, which is fragile and harder to review.
findings.fix: Consider one of these alternatives: (1) Split TabKind into two parts — add `enum TabKind { case file }` in Task 2 (no insight case), then Task 4 extends it with `case insight(InsightSession)` after the real class exists. (2) Defer the entire TabKind addition to Task 4 alongside InsightSession creation. Either approach removes the need for a placeholder + destructive removal. If neither is acceptable for reasons not visible in the task, document the trade-off explicitly.

findings.issue: Task 5 bundles many distinct concerns into one task: (1) DOM template + state extension, (2) markdown-it reconfiguration with link sanitization, (3) CSP meta tag, (4) setText utility, (5) marker parser, (6) debounced re-render, (7) per-block Mermaid pipeline with try/catch + securityLevel:strict, (8) five button handlers, (9) five window setter functions, (10) mode switching integration, (11) commit five fixture files. The task modifies one large file (index.html) but spans many distinct features. Acceptance Criteria has 14 items. This is borderline split candidate. The 'logical cohesion' here is 'insight-mode in WebView', but the security layer (Decision 10 items 1-4: html:false, link sanitizer, CSP, mermaid strict, per-block try/catch) could be cleanly split from the UI layer (DOM template, debounced render, button handlers, window setters, marker parser, fixtures).
findings.fix: Consider splitting into Task 5a (Insight-mode UI: DOM, state, mode switching, button handlers, window setters, debounced render, marker parser, fixtures) and Task 5b (Insight-mode security layer: html:false markdown-it config, link sanitizer, CSP meta, mermaid strict, per-block try/catch, setText utility). If kept as one task, document the cohesion explicitly in Description.
